old: Technique: The box slides with the puck rather than rotating
new: Technique: A box kill slides with the puck rather than rotating
note: Voiced alone, contradicts defensive_zone_coverage.md:367/:371, where the Box+1 box rotates one position behind the +1. Box+1 is the stated rec and beginner default (dzc:372, :380-382), so a rec player hears the opposite instruction for the shape they actually play. W588 named the Position: line ('A box kill is') but left this sibling.

old: **Both high forwards in a box drifting to the same side.** The box **slides** with the puck as a unit; it does not rotate or bunch.
new: **Both high forwards in a box kill drifting to the same side.** The kill box **slides** with the puck as a unit; it does not rotate or bunch.
note: Same contradiction as :513, in a CM bullet. The H3 'Killing with effort instead of with discipline' (:1240) heads the list, but the bullet itself never says kill, and four bullets sit between it and the heading. Even-strength Box+1 has two high players too (dzc:367), so 'does not rotate' applies cleanly to the wrong shape.

old: Convention: The "+1" is the only player who chases the puck; when the puck moves, the role passes to whoever is nearest and the box rotates one position to fill the space
new: Convention: In Box+1, the "+1" is the only player who chases the puck; when the puck moves, the role passes to whoever is nearest and the box rotates one position to fill the space
note: The same clash from the other side. Voiced alone, both '+1' (also the wedge+1 kill term, special_teams:568-569) and 'the box' are bare, and it tells a killer the box rotates, which special_teams:513/:526/:1244 forbid. Adds 12 chars; run check_facts --near first.

old: Convention: Four players form a box around the slot — two low near the posts, two higher near the tops of the circles
new: Convention: In Box+1, four players form a box around the slot — two low near the posts, two higher near the tops of the circles
note: Voiced alone, this is almost word for word the penalty-kill box (special_teams:509). Nothing in the line says Box+1.

old: Key: Not a penalty-kill box — that is four players, two high and two low; Box+1 is a five-player even-strength shape
new: SKETCH: Key: Not a penalty-kill box — a kill's box slides as one unit; Box+1 is a five-player even-strength shape whose box rotates behind a +1 chaser
note: The difference it gives does not separate the two: Box+1's own box is also four players, two high and two low (:370). The difference that changes what a player does, slide vs rotate, is never stated, and that is the Tier 1 clash. The sketch's tactical wording is UNVERIFIED against sources; the writer must check special_teams:526 and dzc:367.

old: Key: The box is the shape almost everyone is taught first
new: Key: The box kill is the penalty-kill shape almost everyone is taught first
note: Voiced alone, it collides with dzc:372: 'Coaching material has Box+1 the standard introductory structure'. Two 'taught first' claims, both about a bare 'box'.

old: Key: Overload — you are usually the lone weak-side outlet
new: Key: Overload power play — you are usually the lone weak-side outlet
note: Defenders also meet the defensive strong-side overload (dzc:116/:128, risk_management Key focus :14, CM :935). There the weak side is abandoned and both D may go low, which is the opposite job. The facts block (:693-699) never says 'power play'; only the H3 does.

old: Key: 2-3 — both defencemen at the points
new: Key: 2-3 power play — both defencemen at the points
note: The 2-3 / left-wing lock forecheck (forechecking_systems:484-506) also holds both D back at the line. Voiced alone, 'the older structure, still common in rec' can attach to either.

old: Position: In a box you are one of the two high players
new: Position: In a box kill you are one of the two high players
note: A centre also plays even-strength Box+1, where the +1 role rotates to whoever is nearest (dzc:367). UNVERIFIED whether a centre is a fixed high player there. Voiced alone, the line does not say kill. The winger twin (:623) is anchored by naming the diamond and wedge+1 in the same line.

old: a 1-3-1 is built around it, an overload usually is not
new: a 1-3-1 power play is built around it, an overload usually is not
note: The body (:237) says '1-3-1 power play'. The facts line drops it, leaving both homonyms bare: 1-3-1 could be neutral zone or forecheck, and overload could be even-strength offensive zone or defensive.

old: Read: On the kill, the player coming out of the box is a fresh attacker
new: Read: On the kill, the player coming out of the penalty box is a fresh attacker
note: Penalty box vs PK box. 'On the kill' primes the formation sense, so 'coming out of the box' can be heard as a killer stepping out of the box shape, which is the very thing the kill teaches against. Body twin :965 is under a clear heading (tier 3).

old: three different formations share these digits

old: an offensive or power-play structure
new: SKETCH: add: Not the same as a defensive strong-side overload, where all five defenders shift to the puck side (Defensive Zone Coverage)
note: The owner entry defines only the attacking sense. The corpus also uses the defensive strong-side overload (dzc:116/:128/:408, risk_management Key focus :14) and 'overload one corner' for the stacked 2-1-2 forecheck (center:406, winger:442, zone_entries:879).

old: Position: In the 1-3-1 you most often play the bumper
new: Position: In the 1-3-1 power play you most often play the bumper

old: Key: 1-3-1 — one defenceman only
new: Key: 1-3-1 power play — one defenceman only

old: Position: In a box you are one of the two high players
